subject: State Eviction and Foreclosure Moratorium Support
overview: In its first remote meeting, the Council addressed emergency COVID-19 measures, rejecting a residential density zoning amendment while passing a resolution to support a statewide moratorium on evictions and foreclosures.

items.title: Alewife Autowork Special Permit
items.summary: Approved a special permit for Class 2 used auto sales and Class 4 auto repair at 33B Mystic Avenue with safety restrictions regarding heavy equipment and a 90-day review.

items.title: Residential Structure Zoning Amendment
items.summary: Rejected a proposed zoning change that would have prohibited two principal residential structures on a single lot, following public opposition and a negative recommendation from the Community Development Board.

items.title: 360 Health and Fitness Extended Hours
items.summary: Approved extended operating hours for a fitness studio at 4110 Mystic Valley Parkway with restrictions attached to the business and a 90-day review.

items.title: El Tecuba Cochina and Tequila Bar Extended Hours
items.summary: Approved extended hours for a restaurant at 31-35 Salem Street, amending the requested 2:00 AM closing to 1:00 AM with a review period starting upon opening.

items.title: National Grid Grant of Location: 2nd Street
items.summary: Approved the installation of an electric conduit on 2nd Street to provide power for improvements at Harris Park.

items.title: National Grid Grant of Location: College Avenue
items.summary: Approved the relocation of gas mains on College Avenue to accommodate construction at Tufts University and the Green Line Extension.

items.title: Establishment of New City Positions
items.summary: Approved on third reading an ordinance establishing the positions of Director of Communications and Director of Community Affairs.

items.title: Winthrop Street Construction Status
items.summary: Requested reports from the building, engineering, and legal departments regarding the status of the stalled Winthrop Street project currently in Land Court.

items.title: Face Surveillance Ban Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed ban on city use of face surveillance technology to the Public Safety Subcommittee for review after the state of emergency.

items.title: State Eviction and Foreclosure Moratorium Support
items.summary: Approved a resolution supporting state house docket 4935 to establish a statewide moratorium on evictions and foreclosures during the pandemic.

items.title: Sanitation and First Responder Safety
items.summary: Requested professional disinfection of public buildings and vehicles and an audit of personal protective equipment for first responders.

items.title: Local Housing Stability Measures
items.summary: Tabled a resolution regarding local rent freezes and restrictions on showing housing units to allow for further review of recent executive orders.

items.title: Donation Collection Bin Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed framework for regulating and permitting donation collection bins to the city solicitor.

items.title: DPW Vehicle Budgetary Transfer
items.summary: Approved a transfer of $102,538 to serve as a match for a state grant to purchase a new trash truck and two dump trucks to replace older diesel vehicles.

items.title: Routine Business and Tabled Items
items.summary: Tabled various committee reports, withdrew a resolution on reusable bags, passed condolences for Larry Rasky, and approved the minutes of the March 10th meeting.
